summary: Zenith Health (security team) reviewed Redwood's encryption at rest/in transit story, BYOK options and HSM integrations. Primary concerns: keys never leaving customer HSM, FIPS/FedRAMP posture, latency impact of remote KMS, audit log retention and syslog integration, and contractual assurances for key custody. Redwood AE+SE explained envelope encryption, optional customer-managed keys, HSM integrations (AWS CloudHSM/GCP HSM), and audit log streaming. Agreed to pilot and run latency benchmarks and share SOC2/ISO artifacts.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Koh (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CISO, Zenith), Nina Patel (Head of Cloud Security), Omar Ruiz (Platform Eng), Lisa Chen (Compliance), Priya Gomez (DevOps)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'm Ava, AE at Redwood, and Daniel's our SE, he'll cover the deep KMS bits.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus here, CISO at Zenith. Big topics: encryption, BYOK, HSMs, and audit logs, want to understand risk model.
[00:20] Nina: Hi, Nina, Cloud Security. We're particularly interested in whether keys ever leave our HSM, and how rotation/audit works.
[00:30] Daniel: Great, we'll walk through our architecture. Quick note - transcript may have some background noise, apologies if audio drops.

[02:15] Daniel: High level: Redwood supports encryption in transit TLS 1.2/1.3, and encryption at rest. For at-rest we use envelope encryption by default; we store data encrypted with a data key and that key is encrypted with a master key in the KMS.
[02:35] Nina: When you say KMS, do you mean Redwood's key store or can we bring our own key? We need BYOK for regulated data.
[02:45] Daniel: Yes, we have several options. Hosted Redwood-managed keys, customer-managed in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and direct HSM integrations via CloudHSM. For BYOK with HSM, Redwood does envelope encryption so we never persist the raw customer master key.

[04:02] Marcus: Important: does the master key material ever leave our HSM or is it exported to Redwood? We need contractual assurance that keys are non-exportable.
[04:12] Daniel: Good question. For CloudHSM and other FIPS HSMs, keys are non-exportable; Redwood receives only encrypted key blobs (wrapped keys). The HSM performs the wrap/unwrap operations. So Redwood never has plaintext root key.
[04:25] Lisa: And what about key rotation? How is rotation orchestrated, and will old data remain decryptable?
[04:34] Ava: Typical flow: you rotate the CMK in your KMS/HSM; Redwood will accept rotated keys and we can rewrap data keys as needed. We support maintaining multiple versions so old data can be decrypted until rewrap completed. We'll document exact steps.

[06:00] Omar: Latency is a concern. If every operation needs an HSM call for unwrap, will inference latency spike? Our SLAs need 200-400ms p50 for small requests.
[06:12] Daniel: Envelope encryption isolates the hot path. Data keys used for encryption/decryption are cached in the runtime for a TTL; plaintext master key unwrap only happens on key rotation or cache miss. For inference, we don't call KMS per token. For BYOK, the initial unwrap is an HSM call but it's not per-request. So steady-state latency impact should be minimal. We'll run benchmarks with your payload to confirm.
[06:45] Nina: Can you support on-prem HSMs or only cloud HSMs? Some of our environments are air-gapped.
[06:55] Daniel: We support private deployments where the control plane is customer-managed; for air-gapped, we offer an on-prem package and can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) if needed. For hosted Redwood, we commonly integrate with AWS CloudHSM or Google Cloud HSM via customer VPC peering.

[09:10] Marcus: Auditability - we need tamper-evident audit logs for key usage, and logs must be shipped into our SIEM. Can Redwood provide per-key usage logs and integrate with syslog/CloudWatch?
[09:22] Ava: Yes, Redwood produces detailed audit logs: key wrap/unwrap events, admin operations, API-level access logs. We can push to CloudWatch logs, CloudTrail, or stream via syslog/forwarders to your SIEM. Retention and retention policies are configurable; we'll align to your compliance needs.

[11:00] Lisa: Are audit logs encrypted at rest, and can we manage their keys as well?
[11:08] Daniel: Audit logs follow the same encryption controls. If you want BYOK for logs, we can apply the same KMS integration so logs are also encrypted with your keys. There's a small operational nuance if you rotate log keys, but manageable.

[13:05] Nina: Certifications - do you have SOC 2 and ISO 27001? Any FedRAMP or FIPS attestations?
[13:12] Ava: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. For FIPS, our HSM integrations rely on underlying HSM FIPS attestations; we can provide documentation. We don't hold a FedRAMP ATO ourselves. We'll share artifacts after the call.

[15:40] Marcus: From a legal standpoint, we need to ensure contractual language for key custody and liability. Has Redwood done BYOK contracts before?
[15:50] Ava: Yes, we have standard BYOK addenda we can share; we also support strict SLA and breach notification terms for enterprise contracts. I'll send the sample language.

[17:00] Omar: Networking: how do you route to our CloudHSM? Do we need to open inbound ports? What's the flow?
[17:08] Daniel: For AWS CloudHSM, we establish VPC peering or use customer VPC endpoints. No inbound internet exposure for the HSM. For private deployments we can colocate in your network and use PKCS#11 over internal network. We'll provide network diagrams.

[19:30] Nina: Curious about key rotation automation. Does Redwood support automatic rotation via KMS policies or does it require manual steps?
[19:40] Daniel: We can tie into your KMS rotation policies; Redwood's integration listens for version changes and can trigger rewrap jobs. There is an option for automatic rewrap or scheduled rewrap windows to avoid noisy re-encryption during peak traffic.

[21:50] Lisa: For compliance, we need separation of duties and RBAC. How granular is Redwood's access control? Can we restrict admins from key operations?
[21:58] Ava: Redwood supports RBAC with roles and permissions, SSO via SAML/Okta, and SCIM provisioning. Admin roles can be restricted from managing keys unless given explicit privileges. For private deployments we can map to your IdP.

[24:00] Marcus: What about multi-region data residency? Some patient data must stay in EU. Can you pin data and keys to regions?
[24:10] Daniel: Yes, we support regional data placement. You can select where data resides and where keys live. For BYOK we recommend keys be in the same region as the data for latency and compliance. We'll note options for cross-region replication with customer approval.

[26:25] Omar: A practical question: during key rotation, is there a window where data is unreadable if rotation fails? What's the rollback story?
[26:33] Daniel: Good question. Our design keeps previous key versions for a configurable grace period. If rewrap fails, we maintain the old wrapped data keys and can rollback. We'll share the exact failure modes and recovery playbook.

[29:00] Nina: Integration testing: we want Redwood to sign a mutual TLS connection and produce signed audit events. Can Redwood produce signed logs and forward to our collector?
[29:10] Ava: We can produce signed log events (e.g., JSON with signatures) and push to your collector. For higher assurance we can set up mTLS for log streaming. We'll scope in the integration deep dive.

[31:40] Marcus: Encryption in transit - you mentioned TLS 1.3. Do you support client certs for API calls?
[31:48] Daniel: Yes, we support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can accept mTLS for private deployments; for hosted APIs we support API keys and mutual TLS via enterprise setup.

[33:20] Nina: On data lifecycle - can Redwood purge data on-demand and provide proof of deletion? We need that for retention and legal requests.
[33:30] Ava: We support configurable retention and deletion APIs; deletion writes are logged and we can provide deletion attestations (hashes/timestamps) for audits. There's also an option to purge cached decrypted material from runtime.

[35:50] Omar: If we go with CloudHSM, we need to know the expected ops: number of unwraps per day, request patterns. Daniel, can you estimate load and what caching TTL you'd recommend?
[36:00] Daniel: For most workloads, we cache plaintext data keys in the runtime for 6-24 hours depending on your security policy; unwraps happen on rotation or when a node boots and cache is empty. For high-churn keys we'd use shorter TTLs. For benchmarks we'll test with your request rate.

[38:10] Lisa: Are there any charges or egress for calling customer's KMS? If we use AWS CloudHSM, will Redwood bill for HSM calls?
[38:20] Ava: Redwood doesn't bill for your KMS calls directly, but the customer will incur CloudHSM costs on their side. For hosted Redwood, we may surface recommended pricing impacts; for Dedicated/Private deployments some infra is part of the contract. We'll clarify in pricing.

[40:00] Marcus: Can you articulate threat model: what attacks are mitigated by BYOK + HSM vs Redwood-managed keys?
[40:10] Daniel: BYOK + HSM ensures that even if Redwood's environment is compromised, attackers cannot decrypt data without access to your HSM. It provides stronger separation of custody and is useful for high-sensitivity data. Redwood-managed keys are simpler but places trust in Redwood's key management. We'll provide a short comparison doc.

[42:30] Nina: Any caveats with third-party libs or open-source runtimes? If Redwood uses third-party cryptography, do you have code attestations?
[42:38] Ava: We use audited crypto libraries; for higher assurance we can provide SBOMs and dependency lists. We don't currently provide full binary attestations by default but can discuss as part of enterprise compliance.

[44:50] Daniel: Quick note on HSM integrations - we support CloudHSM (PKCS#11), Google Cloud HSM, and customer PKCS#11. For some HSM vendors there are network constraints; we'll document and test.

[46:15] Marcus: Ok sounds good. Let's make the pilot plan: we want a small pilot that proves keys never leave HSM, measures latency under our traffic, and validates log delivery to our SIEM.

[46:25] Ava: Agreed. Proposed timeline: security packet today, benchmark in 48 hours, technical deep dive early next week, pilot kickoff within 2 weeks.

[48:40] Lisa: Quick question - can Redwood redact PII from logs before shipping to our SIEM? We sometimes want redacted audit details.

[48:50] Daniel: Yes, we have log redaction rules and can filter sensitive fields prior to forwarding. That can be configured per-route.

[50:05] Omar: One more ops question: who has admin access to key operations in Redwood? Can we enforce MFA and privileged access reviews?

[50:14] Ava: Yes, RBAC + enforced MFA for admin roles, audit of privileged access. We can do periodic access reviews and integrate with your IdP for SSO/SAML.

[51:10] Ava: Recap of next steps: I'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts and sample BYOK contract language; Daniel will run the BYOK latency benchmark and share results; Omar will provide CloudHSM details; Lisa will share log retention and redaction requirements. We'll schedule the deep technical session for next week.

[51:35] Marcus: Thanks everyone. Good meeting.

[52:00] -- End of call --
